children: The euro area's benchmark Bund yields dropped on Thursday as investors rushed into safe-haven assets after tech stocks tumbled overnight while catching up with an overnight decline in US Treasury yields.
Tech stocks took a beating and credit markets wobbled on Thursday as crowded bets on data centres and other AI infrastructure faced a reckoning from high interest rates.
Germany’s 10-year government bond yields (DE10YT=RR), the euro zone benchmark, were down 6.5 basis points to 3.40%. They have moved between about 3.40% and 3.50% since early this month.
Oil prices fell more than 1% as investors weighed risks to supply against US efforts to cut petroleum shipping costs by easing sanctions on so-called shadow fleet vessels.
The German 2-year government bond yield (DE2YT=RR), more sensitive to policy rate expectations, fell 4 bps to 3.06%.
Money markets priced in a depo rate at 3.21% by late 2027, from the current 2.50%, and at 2.73% by December.
The yield gap between French OATs and German Bunds (DE10FR10=RR) was roughly unchanged at 142 bps, after hitting 158.67 in early October, the highest level since November 2011.
The Italian spread (DE10IT10=RR) rose 3 bps to 111 bps, after reaching 129.74 early this month, the widest since April 2025.
